image_description: A black cast-iron skillet containing a cluster of small, round, orange-yellow objects (resembling mini pancakes or cereal puffs). The pan sits on a white stovetop surface. In the background, there is a metallic pot lid and a bunch of bananas to the right.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The black surface of the pan lacks the micro-scratches, oil pooling, or uneven seasoning typically seen in real cast iron. It appears overly uniform and 'matte plastic-like' rather than metallic/seasoned.
The rim thickness appears inconsistent. On the left, the edge seems to thin out and blend slightly into the background/stovetop, lacking a sharp, rigid physical boundary.
The bananas appear slightly warped and lack clear definition, blending into the background in a way that suggests weak geometric grounding.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is taxonomically a frying pan and not a similar kitchen vessel.
To verify the structural integrity of the pan's edge and ensure the handle is physically connected without melting artifacts.
To analyze the material realism of the pan's interior surface and detect subtle AI-generated smoothness or noise patterns.
To ensure the pan sits correctly on the stovetop with proper occlusion and depth separation from the background items.

focus_areas: Material realism of the pan interior (seasoning vs. flat color)
Sharpness and continuity of the pan rim
Physical connection between handle and pan body
Geometric consistency of the circular shape
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the pan's interior. Real cast iron usually has specular highlights from oil or uneven seasoning. If the surface is perfectly matte and uniform, it is likely an artifact. Also, check the rim for 'soft' edges that bleed into the background.
